title: Wire Fraud and Identity Theft Conviction
description: Former Representative Santos pleaded guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft charges. He admitted to stealing donor identities and charging their credit cards without authorization, then transferring funds to his personal account. He also confessed to lying on House financial disclosure forms and falsifying campaign finance reports.

sources.title: George Santos Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud and Identity Theft
Santos Admits to Defrauding Donors, Lying to Congress
United States v. George Anthony Devolder Santos
sources.publication: U.S. District Court, Eastern District of New York

outcome: Guilty plea; expelled from Congress; awaiting sentencing

title: Federal Bribery and Corruption Indictment
description: Senator Menendez was indicted on federal corruption charges including conspiracy to commit bribery, conspiracy to commit honest services fraud, and conspiracy to commit extortion. Prosecutors allege he accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes, including gold bars and cash, in exchange for using his influence to benefit Egyptian government officials and three New Jersey businessmen.

sources.title: United States v. Robert Menendez, Nadine Menendez, et al.
sources.publication: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York

sources.title: Senator Robert Menendez Charged With Corruption
Menendez Indicted on Federal Bribery Charges

outcome: Trial pending; senator has pleaded not guilty

title: House Ethics Investigation into Stock Trades
description: The House Ethics Committee announced an investigation into Rep. Curtis for potential violations of the STOCK Act and financial disclosure requirements. The probe focuses on whether Curtis failed to properly disclose stock transactions and whether any trades violated conflict-of-interest rules related to his committee assignments.

sources.title: Statement by the Committee on Ethics
House Ethics Panel Investigating Rep. John Curtis Over Stock Trades

title: DUI Conviction
description: Senator Crapo pleaded guilty to driving under the influence after being arrested in Alexandria, Virginia with a blood alcohol level of 0.11%. He was sentenced to 180 days in jail (suspended) and fined $250. Crapo publicly apologized and stated he had stopped drinking alcohol.

sources.title: Idaho Sen. Crapo Pleads Guilty to DUI
Case No. GC12015942-00
Sen. Mike Crapo Arrested on DUI Charge

outcome: Guilty plea, fine, license suspension, completed sentence

title: Bribery and Money Laundering Indictment
description: Rep. Cuellar and his wife were indicted on conspiracy and bribery charges, accused of accepting $600,000 in bribes from an Azerbaijan state-owned oil company and a Mexican bank in exchange for using his office to influence U.S. policy. The indictment alleges laundering of bribe payments through shell companies and front organizations.

sources.title: United States v. Henry Cuellar and Imelda Cuellar
sources.publication: U.S. District Court, Southern District of Texas

sources.title: Rep. Henry Cuellar and Wife Indicted on Bribery Charges
Texas Democrat Cuellar Charged in Foreign Bribery Scheme

outcome: Trial scheduled; defendants pleaded not guilty

title: Campaign Finance Violation
description: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez was found to have violated campaign finance rules by improperly using campaign funds for personal expenses. The House Ethics Committee issued a formal admonishment after determining she used campaign funds to pay for childcare expenses and failed to properly reimburse the campaign.

sources.title: Report Concerning Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Admonished for Campaign Finance Violation

title: Sexual Harassment Allegations
description: Multiple former staffers alleged inappropriate workplace conduct by Rep. Brecheen, including unwanted sexual advances and creating a hostile work environment. The allegations were reported by three independent news organizations based on interviews with former employees. Brecheen denied the allegations and no formal investigation was announced.

sources.title: Former Staffers Accuse Rep. Brecheen of Sexual Harassment
Multiple Women Allege Misconduct by Oklahoma Congressman
Oklahoma Rep. Faces Workplace Harassment Claims

outcome: Allegations based on media reports; no formal investigation announced

title: DOJ Insider Trading Investigation
description: The Department of Justice opened an investigation into potential insider trading by Rep. Thompson, focusing on stock trades made prior to public announcements affecting agricultural and energy sectors. The investigation examines whether Thompson used non-public information obtained through his position as Agriculture Committee Chairman to make profitable trades.

sources.title: DOJ Investigating Rep. Thompson for Potential Insider Trading
Pennsylvania Congressman Under Federal Investigation
Ag Committee Chair Faces Insider Trading Probe

title: Manhattan Criminal Indictment — Falsifying Business Records
description: A Manhattan grand jury indicted former President Trump on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to conceal hush money payments to adult film actress Stormy Daniels ahead of the 2016 election. Trump was convicted on all 34 counts in May 2024.

sources.title: People of the State of New York v. Donald J. Trump
Trump Found Guilty on All 34 Felony Counts
Trump Convicted in Historic Criminal Trial

outcome: Convicted on all 34 felony counts; sentencing pending

title: Federal Classified Documents Indictment
description: A federal grand jury indicted Trump on 37 counts related to willful retention of national defense information and obstruction. Prosecutors alleged Trump kept classified documents at Mar-a-Lago after leaving office and obstructed efforts to retrieve them. Case was dismissed by Judge Cannon citing special counsel appointment issues.

sources.title: United States v. Donald J. Trump
sources.publication: U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida

sources.title: Trump Indicted on Federal Charges Over Classified Documents

outcome: Dismissed by Judge Cannon; DOJ appealed

title: Federal Election Interference Indictment
description: Special Counsel Jack Smith obtained a federal indictment charging Trump with conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to obstruct an official proceeding, obstruction of an official proceeding, and conspiracy against rights. The charges stemmed from efforts to overturn the 2020 election results, including the January 6th Capitol breach.

sources.title: United States v. Donald J. Trump
sources.publication: U.S. District Court, District of Columbia

sources.title: Trump Indicted Over Efforts to Overturn 2020 Election

outcome: Dropped after Trump won 2024 election per DOJ policy

title: Georgia RICO Election Interference Indictment
description: A Fulton County grand jury indicted Trump and 18 co-defendants under Georgia RICO statutes for allegedly conspiring to overturn the 2020 election results in Georgia. The charges included the infamous phone call asking Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger to "find 11,780 votes."

sources.title: State of Georgia v. Donald John Trump et al.
Trump and Allies Charged in Georgia Election Case

outcome: Case ongoing; multiple co-defendants have taken plea deals

title: New York Civil Fraud Judgment — $454 Million
description: Judge Arthur Engoron found Trump liable for persistent fraud in a civil case brought by NY Attorney General Letitia James. The ruling determined Trump inflated his net worth by billions of dollars to obtain favorable loans and insurance. Trump was ordered to pay $454 million in penalties and disgorgement.

sources.title: People of the State of New York v. Trump Organization et al.
Trump Ordered to Pay $454 Million in New York Fraud Case
